L001: [Profile] Alex Zhang | University Junior, E-Commerce Major
L002: [Target Role] AI Application Product Manager Intern
L003: 
L004: [Personal Project] Campus Lost & Found LLM Q&A Bot (2025.09 - 2025.11)
L005: 1. Identified pain point of fragmented lost & found notices on campus forums; built automated Q&A WeChat bot.
L006: 2. Authored structured extraction prompt parsing item type, lost location, time, and distinctive features from forum posts.
L007: 3. Tested prompt across 120 historical lost-and-found posts; identified recurring location extraction errors.
L008: 4. Added campus building alias lookup dictionary as few-shot constraints into prompt, improving extraction accuracy.
L009: 5. Limitation: Did not build automated test script; manually verified 30 sample responses to evaluate accuracy.
L010: 
L011: [Skills]
L012: - Proficient with ChatGPT, Claude, and Kimi; experienced with system prompt engineering.
L013: - Basic Python scripting for web scraping and text cleaning.

expectedDiagnosis.reasons: Constructed structured extraction prompts and injected campus alias dictionaries to constrain output.
Identified location errors on 120 samples, but lacked systematic taxonomy or root cause categorization.
Applicant candidly noted manual check of only 30 samples; lacks formal evaluation harness.
No mentions of model fine-tuning; null competence applied with zero penalty.

expectedInterviewQuestions: In your Lost & Found bot, you manually inspected 30 samples. If scaling to 5,000 inquiries, how would you design an automated evaluation metric like Precision or Recall?
When you identified recurring location extraction errors, what steps did you take to categorize and debug the root causes?
How did you evaluate whether the building alias dictionary covered rare or informal campus nicknames?
